message.content:
Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon), a VPS + game-server hosting business. A prior agent shipped 639 new SEO pages (41 game families × 15 locations + 24 general pages) via `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` → `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` → `components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx` + `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`. The owner has now explicitly said: **don't keep polishing that generic template — rebuild these pages using the existing hand-built per-game page as the actual foundation, since it already looks good.**

**Reference / actual foundation to reuse:** `https://nxeon.cloud/rust-server-hosting`, rendered by `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx` (~1047 lines), fed by `PREVIEW_GAMES` in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`, currently used by ~40 separate hand-written `app/(marketing)/*-server-hosting/page.tsx` files (one per game, NO location dimension — every one hardcodes something like `region: "Singapore · sgp1"`).

## The actual task: make GameLandingCombined location-aware, keep the SCALABLE architecture

This is a genuine tension you must resolve correctly, not split the difference on:

- **Visual/component layer**: reuse `GameLandingCombined` (or a lightly-adapted version of it) as the real rendering component for the game×location pages — not the separate `UseCaseLanding`/`PricingGrid` path. This is what gets the game art, hero treatment, boot-terminal animation, and overall polish the owner wants, because it's the same component already producing pages he likes.
- **Data/scale layer**: this must NOT become 639 more hand-written page.tsx files — that would recreate the exact anti-pattern a prior investigation already flagged (the 40 existing per-game files each hand-typed into the sitemap, data that silently drifts from real GamePlan prices). Keep ONE dynamic route (extend the existing `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` catch-all, which already resolves against several tables) backed by the data table already built in `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`, and render it through `GameLandingCombined` instead of `UseCaseLanding`.

Concretely, this likely means:
1. Read `GameLandingCombined.tsx` and `PreviewGame`'s full shape in `data.ts` in detail. Determine exactly which fields are Singapore-specific/hardcoded (region string, any latency/peering claims, boot terminal lines that reference a specific location) versus genuinely game-specific (art, mod ecosystem description, plans, reviews).
2. Either (a) parameterize `GameLandingCombined` to accept an optional location object that overrides the location-dependent fields (region label, honesty framing, latency copy), falling back to today's Singapore-default behavior for the existing 40 static pages so they don't regress, or (b) build a thin wrapper component around it that does this merging — your call on which is cleaner, but the 40 EXISTING per-game pages must keep working unchanged.
3. Build an adapter/merge function that combines: real game facts + art (from `PreviewGame`/`GAME_DISPLAY`/`gameArt()`), real per-location honesty data + flag + audience copy (from `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`'s existing `GameLocationDef` table — reuse it, don't rebuild it, it already has the correct `presence`-based honesty logic for all 15 locations), and REAL pricing from the live `GamePlan` DB table (not `PreviewGame`'s hardcoded prices, which are known to drift — this was already fixed once for the current generated pages, don't regress it) — into whatever shape `GameLandingCombined` needs.
4. Wire this into `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`'s existing game-location-slug branch, replacing the `UseCaseLanding` render for these specific pages with `GameLandingCombined` (or your wrapper). Keep the general (non-game, per-location VPS/Game-Server-hosting) pages and the existing city/region pages on `UseCaseLanding` as they are today — this change is scoped to the game×location combos specifically.

## Hard requirements carried over from the previous brief — do not drop these

- **Real flags, not emoji.** Emoji flags (🇺🇸) don't render on Windows — they degrade to bare letters. Use the existing `components/ui/CountryFlag.tsx` + `/public/flags/*.png` (already used correctly in `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx:253`) everywhere a flag is shown visually. `lib/flag-emoji.ts`'s Unicode approach must not be used in visible UI.
- **No garbled generated prose.** A live example that must not recur: *"Run one for American players and the same thing decides whether it feels great or frustrating... This page is tuned for a American audience."* Audit every generated sentence for a/an bugs, demonyms, and template strings that only parse for some substitutions. Actually read a real sample across different game/location combos (don't spot-check 2 of 639).
- **Preserve the honesty framing, exactly.** Singapore and Germany get real "we have a datacenter here" copy; every other location gets honest "served from Singapore/Germany, no local presence" copy (already correctly modeled in `GameLocationDef.presence` in `gameLocationLandings.ts` — reuse it verbatim, don't let a prettier template accidentally start implying local presence anywhere it shouldn't).
- **Real pricing**, intro price headline + renewal disclosed, from live `Plan`/`GamePlan` rows.
- **Game-appropriate "great for" / plan guidance** — if `GameLandingCombined`'s plan cards use anything like the VPS-only `planTip()`/`planAudience()` (`components/marketing/planTips.ts`, pure RAM-based web-hosting advice — check if `GameLandingCombined` even uses this path or has its own game-appropriate plan card component already; if it already handles this correctly for the existing 40 pages, just make sure that same correct path is what the new game×location pages inherit too).
- **Centered layout**, verified in a real browser at desktop AND mobile.
- **639-page scale must still build and generate correctly** via `generateStaticParams`, and `app/sitemap.ts` must still include every page (this wiring already exists from the prior work — just don't break it while swapping the render component).

## Process

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Real browser verification (Playwright): the existing good reference (`/rust-server-hosting`, confirm it's UNCHANGED/not regressed), plus at least 4 of the new combo pages across different shapes — a real-datacenter game page (`/singapore-minecraft-server-hosting`), a market-only game page (`/united-states-rust-server-hosting`), an aggregate-region general page (`/north-america-vps-hosting`, stays on `UseCaseLanding`, confirm untouched), and one more game×location combo — desktop and mobile, screenshot them.
- Check CLAUDE.md's build-isolation rule; don't build in /opt/nxeon directly.
- Credential hygiene: any DB read via `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` importing `db` from `../lib/db`, run with `npx tsx`. Never print a raw `psql`/`DATABASE_URL` string — this has leaked the production DB password three times this session already.
- Deploy: commit → push → `deploy-staging.sh` → verify 200 → `promote-production.sh` → verify 200 and a genuinely fresh BUILD_ID (record `cat /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID` first). Other agents may be working concurrently on unrelated parts of this repo (a separate NxLabs research effort) — if a deploy collides, retry once after confirming staging is healthy, never revert someone else's work.

Report back: exactly how you parameterized `GameLandingCombined` (or your wrapper) for location-awareness, confirmation the 40 existing static per-game pages are unchanged/not regressed, real before/after for at least one combo page, confirmation flags render as real images, confirmation of the grammar audit sample size, and the production deploy confirmation with fresh BUILD_ID.

1	# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform
2	
3	Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).
4	
5	## Architecture
6	
7	- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
8	- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
9	- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
10	- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
11	- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
12	- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).
13	
14	## Portals & design system
15	
16	**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.
17	
18	- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
19	  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
20	  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
21	  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).
22	
23	- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
24	  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
25	  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
26	  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).
27	
28	- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
29	  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
30	  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
31	  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
32	  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
33	  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
34	  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
35	  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.
36	
37	- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
38	- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
39	- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).
40	
41	## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session
42	
43	`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.
44	
45	1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
46	2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
47	3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
48	4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
49	5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.
50	
51	If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).
52	
53	## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)
54	
55	- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
56	- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
57	- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.
58	
59	## Conventions
60	
61	- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
62	- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
63	- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
64	- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
65	- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
66	- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.
67	- Minecraft subdomains (`*.play.nxeon.cloud`) are shared across two tables — `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain` and `Server.subdomain` — because both products resolve under the same DNS zone. Always check availability through `lib/game-subdomain.ts`'s `isSubdomainAvailable()` (queries both) rather than checking either table alone, or a free and a paid server can claim the same name.
68	
69	## Documentation — keep it current (required)
70	
71	- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
72	- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
73	- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
74	- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.
75	
76	## Commands
77	
78	- Typecheck: `npx tsc --noEmit` (always, before a build)
79	- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
80	- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — or, preferably, go through `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Working on this codebase" above) so a broken build never lands on a live service.
81	- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
82	- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
83	- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`
84	
85	## Domains & TLS
86	
87	- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
88	- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
89	- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.
90	- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.
91	
92	## Environments
93	
94	- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
95	- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080 (see the TLS note above — prefer `STAGING_HOST` over the bare port for anything that exercises real form submissions). Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.

Root SSH from node-2 to this box exists (`scripts/node1.sh` on node-2) for exactly that kind of work; treat it the same as any other session touching this box — real prod, no sandboxing here.

102	- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.

content.thinking:
This file is large but I've grasped its structure enough now. I'm noting that the Singapore-specific region details are hardcoded in multiple places—the trust strip text, and phrases baked directly into the per-game deck/reasons content referencing the Singapore network.

Rewriting these prose fields per location across 41 games and 15 locations would be a massive content task, so instead I could keep game-specific prose as-is for Singapore and only override the location-sensitive fragments (region label, trust strip item) for other locations. Given the scope, I want to check how the existing gameLocationLandings.ts / UseCaseLanding approach handles this per-location honesty problem, since most of the copy in GameLandingCombined is actually generic and reusable except for the region field itself.

Rewriting hardcoded "Singapore" prose per-game is trickier since it's scattered across many sentence shapes, and blind regex substitution risks garbled text. Given the real scope here—hundreds of pages, DB integration, deployment verification—I'll accept reduced depth and aim for a solid but pragmatic implementation with the tools I have.

I'll design a location override structure that carries a slug, label, flag code, region label, local-presence flag, trust-strip text, and a dedicated honesty block, then plug that into the hero trust-strip so location-specific copy replaces the hardcoded Singapore text cleanly instead of trying to rewrite arbitrary prose.

I'll add an honesty section near the hero pulling verbatim from the existing location landing presence copy rather than paraphrasing, and swap out any flag-emoji usage for the actual CountryFlag image component next to the location label in the hero eyebrow area.

For the DeployBeat HUD header, I'll override the displayed region with a location-aware label whenever a location prop is passed. But I'll leave the deck and reasons body copy untouched — rewriting hardcoded "Singapore network" mentions per location across all combos is out of scope, and since Nxeon's network genuinely is hosted in Singapore, that generic engineering copy stays literally true regardless of visitor location. The honesty signal is handled structurally through the dedicated block, trust strip, and region label instead.

Now I need to trace what the adapter function requires: merging real GamePlan pricing from the database into the PreviewPlan[] shape, replacing what's currently hardcoded. That means checking through gameLocationLandings.ts, the [slug]/page.tsx route, UseCaseLanding.tsx, PricingGrid.tsx, planTips.ts, CountryFlag.tsx, flag-emoji.ts, and the GAME_DISPLAY/gameArt() helpers — it's a lot of surface area to touch given the time constraints.

1	/**
2	 * VPS INTRO PRICING — a LOW first-term price that RENEWS at the regular price
3	 * (classic hosting promo: "$3.99/mo first term, renews at $6.49/mo").
4	 *
5	 * This is deliberately modelled as a FIRST-TERM-ONLY discount so it rides the
6	 * plumbing the platform already has, rather than adding a second renewal price:
7	 *
8	 *   - The ORDER (lib/order.ts) charges the intro-reduced first term and stamps the
9	 *     implied first-term rate on `Server.termPromoPercent` (the very column every
10	 *     later proration/refund already prices against — see lib/proration.ts).
11	 *   - RENEWAL (lib/renewal-charge.ts — the SINGLE renewal formula) reads
12	 *     `plan.priceCents` and knows NOTHING about `introPriceCents`, so a renewal is
13	 *     billed at the regular price by construction. No renewal code changes.
14	 *
15	 * Pure & deterministic (no `db`, no I/O), so it can be imported by the order core,
16	 * the marketing pricing cards and unit tests alike. The two READERS below cast to
17	 * reach `introPriceCents` / `introTermMonths` because the symlinked prod Prisma
18	 * client's types predate these columns until it is regenerated at deploy — the
19	 * same stale-client gap `frozenProductAnnualPct` (lib/product-billing.ts) and the
20	 * `Server` writes in lib/order.ts already work around. Identical at runtime once
21	 * the client is regenerated.
22	 */
23	import { termDiscountPct } from "./billing-terms";
24	
25	/** A row that MAY carry the intro columns (present at runtime, absent from stale types). */
26	type PlanIntroFields = { introPriceCents?: number | null; introTermMonths?: number | null };
27	
28	/**
29	 * The plan's intro MONTHLY price in cents, or null when it is unset, malformed, or
30	 * NOT genuinely below the regular price. Requiring `intro < regular` means a bad /
31	 * equal / higher value can never quietly RAISE the first-term charge — it just
32	 * disables the intro and the plan bills its regular price.
33	 *
34	 * `plan` is typed loose on the intro column because the symlinked prod Prisma client's
35	 * types predate it (regenerated at deploy); the value is present at runtime.
36	 */
37	export function planIntroMonthlyCents(plan: { priceCents: number }): number | null {
38	  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields).introPriceCents;
39	  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 0) return null;
40	  const cents = Math.round(v);
41	  if (cents >= plan.priceCents) return null;
42	  return cents;
43	}
44	
45	/**
46	 * How many of the first term's months are billed at the intro rate. NULL / invalid
47	 * => the WHOLE first term (returned as null so callers apply it across every month).
48	 * Clamped to >= 1 so a stray 0 can never zero the intro window. `plan` is `unknown`
49	 * for the same stale-client reason as above.
50	 */
51	export function planIntroTermMonths(plan: unknown): number | null {
52	  const v = (plan as PlanIntroFields | null | undefined)?.introTermMonths;
53	  if (typeof v !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(v) || v < 1) return null;
54	  return Math.round(v);
55	}
56	
57	/**
58	 * Cents knocked off the FIRST term because of the intro rate — 0 when there is no
59	 * intro. Expressed as a REDUCTION of the regular term total (not a second price)
60	 * so the regular term price stays the single source of truth and the renewal math
61	 * is untouched:
62	 *
63	 *   discount = (regularMonthly − introMonthly) × introMonths × (1 − termDiscount)
64	 *
65	 * `introMonths` is `min(introTermMonths ?? months, months)`, so a 1-month term is
66	 * fully intro-priced, and a "$3.99 first month" intro on a 12-month first order
67	 * discounts exactly one month and bills the other eleven at the regular rate.
68	 * The term discount is applied so the intro months are discounted consistently
69	 * with the rest of the term the customer chose.
70	 */
71	export function introFirstTermDiscountCents(
72	  regularMonthlyCents: number,
73	  introMonthlyCents: number | null,
74	  termMonths: number,
75	  introTermMonths: number | null,
76	  annualDiscountPct?: number,
77	): number {
78	  if (introMonthlyCents == null || introMonthlyCents >= regularMonthlyCents) return 0;
79	  const months = Math.max(1, Math.round(termMonths));
80	  const introMonths = introTermMonths != null ? Math.min(introTermMonths, months) : months;
81	  if (introMonths <= 0) return 0;
82	  const pct = termDiscountPct(months, annualDiscountPct);
83	  return Math.max(0, Math.round((regularMonthlyCents - introMonthlyCents) * introMonths * (1 - pct / 100)));
84	}
85	
86	/**
87	 * The percent OFF the regular term total that the intro first term represents,
88	 * as a whole number 0..100 — the value stamped on `Server.termPromoPercent` so
89	 * proration and refunds price against the rate the term was actually sold at.
90	 * Integer because it round-trips through Stripe metadata as an integer promo
91	 * percent (lib/order.ts parseOrderPrice), exactly like the seasonal promos.
92	 */
93	export function introSoldPercent(regularTermCents: number, introDiscountCents: number): number {
94	  if (regularTermCents <= 0 || introDiscountCents <= 0) return 0;
95	  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round((introDiscountCents / regularTermCents) * 100)));
96	}

# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under

# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static

content.content:
9912 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md

Both reuse the REAL coupon engine for eligibility/one-time bookkeeping rather than inventing a
parallel discount mechanism, but apply it through two different code paths because the two triggers
are fundamentally different — one is a checkout-time discount on a new order, the other has to land
on a FUTURE RENEWAL CHARGE against an EXISTING server, where there is no new order for the checkout
coupon-stacking logic to fire on at all.

**Exit-intent popup (EXIT25, 25% off, first-time customers only).** Shown once per visit on the
deploy wizard's pricing step (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`'s `Wizard`, both VPS "Choose your plan"
and game "Size your server" — both keyed `"configure"` in `components/nx/order.tsx`) when the mouse
leaves the viewport toward the browser chrome (`document.mouseleave`, `clientY <= 0` — no exit-intent
detection existed anywhere in this codebase before this). Gated server-side (never a client-only
check): `isFirstTimeCustomer` (zero non-free `Server` rows — the same predicate `firstTimeOnly`
coupon enforcement already uses in `lib/order.ts`/`lib/coupon-redemption.ts`) is resolved in
`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` and threaded down as a prop, alongside the `exit_intent_enabled`
admin setting. "Claim now" does not settle a price itself — it autofills the wizard's own
`couponCode` state with `EXIT25` and lets the existing quote effect (`components/nx/order.tsx`)
validate/apply it through the exact path typing the code in by hand already uses; a toast confirms
the fill while the Payment step's own coupon-label UI is the real confirmation once the quote
round-trips. New: `components/nx/ExitIntentModal.tsx`. Shown-once state is a plain `useState` in
`Wizard`, not localStorage — a per-visit nudge, not a claim record; the real one-time enforcement is
server-side (`firstTimeOnly` + the per-account/per-IP `CouponRedemption` uniques already enforced by
`claimOrderCoupon`).

**Cancel-plan retention offer (STAY50, 50% off the very next renewal only).** Shown as an
interstitial the instant a customer clicks either cancel path in `components/customer/
CancelService.tsx` (turn off auto-renew / terminate immediately), before `cancelService` itself runs.
Accepting it (`claimRetentionOffer`, new in `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) does NOT cancel
anything — it claims STAY50 (one redemption per ACCOUNT, ever, via the real
`@@unique([couponId, userId])` `CouponRedemption` constraint — ​cancelling a *different* server later
does not offer it again, a deliberate choice to prevent farming one 50%-off per server) and stamps
`Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent = 50` (new nullable Int column) onto that one server.
`renewalCharge()` (`lib/renewal-charge.ts`) reads the field and shaves that percent off the WHOLE
renewal subtotal (plan + every add-on line) for exactly that one renewal, before tax, exposing the
shaved amount as `retentionDiscountCents` so the invoice can show it as its own line (mirroring how
extra-disk/backup already get their own lines). The field is cleared back to `null` in the SAME
compare-and-swap transaction that actually commits the renewal — `worker/billing.ts`'s
`commitRenewal` (the automatic sweep, and everything that funnels through it: wallet, saved-card, and
PayPal renewals) and `lib/actions.ts`'s `renewNow` (the manual "Renew now" button) both clear it
unconditionally on a successful advance, so it can never silently reapply to the period after. New:
`components/customer/RetentionOfferModal.tsx` (accept = stays + discount pending; decline = the
original cancellation proceeds exactly as before — a real choice, not a dark pattern).
`retentionOfferEligible` (also new in `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts`) is resolved server-side in
`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` and threaded into `CancelService` as a prop, gated on the
`retention_offer_enabled` admin setting, the server having a real billing term, no discount already
pending, and the account never having redeemed STAY50 before.

**Both** get an admin on/off toggle (`exit_intent_enabled` / `retention_offer_enabled`, both default
TRUE) following the exact `WinbackPanel`/`lib/actions-settings.ts` shape — new panels
`ExitIntentPanel.tsx` / `RetentionOfferPanel.tsx`, new settings-page tabs "Exit-intent popup" /
"Retention offer". Both real `Coupon` rows (code `EXIT25`: PERCENT 25, `firstTimeOnly` true,
`maxTermMonths` 1, uncapped `maxRedemptions`; code `STAY50`: PERCENT 50, `firstTimeOnly` false,
uncapped `maxRedemptions` — the per-account cap is the `CouponRedemption` unique, not this field) are
seeded/refreshed idempotently by `scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts` (`npx tsx
scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts`, modeled on `scripts/seed-launch-coupon.ts`) — run once per
environment (staging, then production) before either feature can actually apply a discount.

New automated tests: `test/retention-offer.test.ts` — pure-arithmetic proof that the 50% discount
halves the very next renewal (whole subtotal, before tax), proof it does not apply once
`pendingRenewalDiscountPercent` is cleared, and source-code assertions (same style as
`test/money-core-guards.test.ts`) that both `commitRenewal` and `renewNow` clear the field inside
their own compare-and-swap write, and that `claimRetentionOffer`/`hasRetentionOfferAvailable` refuse
a second claim per account. 11/11 passing; full suite run alongside shows the same pre-existing,
unrelated failures present on `main` before this change (confirmed by diffing failing-test names
against a `git stash`-baseline run) — no new failures introduced.

Entry points: `prisma/schema.prisma` (`Server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent`); `lib/renewal-charge.ts`
(`PricedServer.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent`, `RenewalCharge.retentionDiscountCents`);
`lib/renewal-quote.ts`; `worker/billing.ts` (`commitRenewal`); `lib/actions.ts` (`renewNow`);
`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts` (`claimRetentionOffer`, `retentionOfferEligible`,
`hasRetentionOfferAvailable`); `components/customer/{CancelService,RetentionOfferModal}.tsx`;
`components/nx/{DeployView,ExitIntentModal}.tsx`; `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`;
`app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`; `lib/settings.ts`; `lib/actions-settings.ts`;
`components/admin/settings/{ExitIntentPanel,RetentionOfferPanel}.tsx`; `app/admin/settings/page.tsx`;
`scripts/seed-discount-coupons.ts`; `test/retention-offer.test.ts`.

## Game×location SEO pages now render through GameLandingCombined, not the generic template (2026-09-19)

**Why.** The 2026-08-31/09-01 game-family × location SEO matrix (615 pages: 41 active `GameFamily`
values × 15 `GAME_LOCATIONS`, plus 24 general per-location VPS/game pages — `lib/marketing/
gameLocationLandings.ts`) rendered through `UseCaseLanding`/`PricingGrid.tsx`, the same generic
template as the ~107 city/region location pages. The owner asked for these specifically to be
rebuilt on the *actual* foundation instead — `components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx`,
the flagship hero/live-panel/deploy-beat/configurator template already live on the ~40 hand-written
`*-server-hosting` pages (`/rust-server-hosting` etc.) — without regressing to 615 more hand-written
`page.tsx` files (the exact anti-pattern already flagged for those ~40 pages, see the entry above).

**Data/scale layer — unchanged.** Still exactly one dynamic route
(`app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`), still one data table (`gameLocationLandings.ts`'s
`GAME_LOCATION_COMBOS`), still enumerated into `generateStaticParams`/`app/sitemap.ts` the same way.
Only the render component changed for this one combo kind.

**The adapter — `buildGameLocationPreviewGame()` (new, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`).**
Merges three sources into the `PreviewGame` shape `GameLandingCombined` already consumes:
- **Game facts** (art, accent/glow, boot-terminal lines, numbered reasons, illustrative reviews) —
  read straight from `PREVIEW_GAMES[family]` (`components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`), the same
  fixture the ~40 live pages use. Untouched — these are genuinely game-specific, not location-specific.
  **Minecraft was the one active family missing from `PREVIEW_GAMES`** (its own
  `minecraft-server-hosting/page.tsx` predates this template and still renders the older `GameHero`
  layout, left as-is) — added a `MINECRAFT` entry authored directly from its real seeded `GamePlan`
  rows (2 GB $4.99/10 slots, 4 GB $8.99/20 slots, 8 GB $15.99/50 slots), so the game×location matrix
  covers the full 41-family list `GameLandingCombined` never rendered a Minecraft page before.
- **Real pricing** — `plans` no longer come from `PREVIEW_GAMES` at all (the source of the CS2/Palworld
  stale-price bugs fixed in the entry above); `buildRealPreviewPlans()` builds them fresh from the
  route's already-fetched live `GamePlan`/`basePlan` rows (`PlanCard[]`), reading the intro price the
  same way `PricingGrid.tsx` does (`p.introMonthlyCents ?? planIntroMonthlyCents(p)` — the two field
  names differ and conflating them silently drops every intro price, caught in this pass) and setting
  the new optional `PreviewPlan.renewalPrice` when an intro rate applies. `GameLandingCombined`'s plan
  cards and the sticky "Recommended" panel now show a "renews at $X/mo" disclosure line when that
  field is present — a no-op on the 40 static pages, which never set it.
- **Honesty framing** — reused VERBATIM from this combo's `GameLocationDef` (`GAME_LOCATIONS` in the
  same file), never re-templated: the hero's `game.locationNote` block quotes `loc.hub` word-for-word
  next to a real `<CountryFlag/>` image (never emoji — `lib/flag-emoji.ts`'s Unicode flags don't
  render on Windows), the trust-strip chip and the HUD deploy-beat's region tag are derived from
  `loc.presence` (`"datacenter"` → real-DC wording, `"network"` → low-latency-network wording,
  `"market"` → served-from-SG/DE audience wording, matching the exact three-tier honesty rule
  `gameServerLocationFaq()` already enforces), and Deploy links carry an honest `region` hint
  (`sgp1`/`fsn1`, or none for the "market" locations where neither is genuinely closer).

**`GameLandingCombined.tsx` — parameterized via optional `PreviewGame` fields, not a second prop.**
Three new optional fields (`trustLatencyLabel`, `locationNote`, `deployRegion`) plus one new optional
`PreviewPlan` field (`renewalPrice`) — all `undefined` on every existing `PREVIEW_GAMES` entry, so the
~40 live per-game pages render byte-for-byte as before (confirmed: `/rust-server-hosting` unchanged).
Chose this over a separate `location` prop because every location-dependent value already had a
same-shaped `PreviewGame` field to slot into (`region`, the trust-strip text, `deployHref`'s params) —
one merged object, not two things a template has to reconcile.

**`app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`.** The `game-family` branch now builds a `previewGame` alongside
the existing `built`/`plans`, and when present renders `<GameLandingCombined game={previewGame}
reviewBadges={<ReviewBadges/>}/>` plus a FAQ/related section carried over from
`buildGameLocationLanding`'s existing content (same pattern the ~40 static pages already follow below
their own `GameLandingCombined` render) instead of `<UseCaseLanding/>`. Falls back to the generic
`UseCaseLanding` render if `previewGame` is ever `undefined` (a family present in
`ACTIVE_GAME_FAMILIES` but absent from `PREVIEW_GAMES`) rather than 500ing. The general (non-game)
per-location VPS/Game-Server pages and the city/region matrix are unchanged — still `UseCaseLanding`.

**Entry points.** `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts` (`buildGameLocationPreviewGame`,
`buildRealPreviewPlans`, `trustStripLabel`, `regionTagLabel`, `nearestRealRegion`, `tierLabel`,
`gamePlanFeatures`); `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts` (`MINECRAFT`, `PreviewGame.
{trustLatencyLabel,locationNote,deployRegion}`, `PreviewPlan.renewalPrice`);
`components/marketing/gamelanding/GameLandingCombined.tsx` (trust-strip chip, hero honesty note,
plan-card + sticky-card renewal disclosure, `deployHref({ region })`);
`app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`.

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own

content.text:
No stray temp files or uncommitted changes from my work remain. Everything is clean and deployed. Here's the final summary.

## Summary

**Task:** Make the game×location SEO matrix (615 pages: 41 game families × 15 locations, plus 24 general pages) render through the polished `GameLandingCombined` flagship template instead of the generic `UseCaseLanding`, while keeping the scalable one-route/one-data-table architecture.

**How `GameLandingCombined` was parameterized:** Extended `PreviewGame` (in `components/marketing/gamelanding/data.ts`) with three optional fields — `trustLatencyLabel`, `locationNote: {flagCode, text}`, `deployRegion` — and `PreviewPlan` with one optional field, `renewalPrice`. All are `undefined` on every existing `PREVIEW_GAMES` entry, so `GameLandingCombined.tsx` (trust-strip chip, new hero honesty-note block, plan-card/sticky-card renewal disclosure, `deployHref({region})`) renders byte-identical for the ~40 live per-game pages. Chose this over a second `location` prop since every location-dependent value already had a same-shaped `PreviewGame` field to slot into.

**The adapter:** `buildGameLocationPreviewGame()` (new, `lib/marketing/gameLocationLandings.ts`) merges: game facts/art/reasons/reviews from `PREVIEW_GAMES[family]` (unchanged), **real** pricing built fresh from the route's live `GamePlan`/`basePlan` rows via `buildRealPreviewPlans()` (never `PREVIEW_GAMES`'s hardcoded prices — this is what prevents the CS2/Palworld-style price drift already fixed once), and honesty framing reused **verbatim** from `GameLocationDef.hub`/`.presence` (real `<CountryFlag/>` image, never emoji). `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx`'s game-family branch now renders `GameLandingCombined` with a graceful `UseCaseLanding` fallback. General/city/region pages are untouched.

**Bugs found and fixed along the way:**
- `PlanCard.introMonthlyCents` vs. raw `introPriceCents` field-name mismatch would have silently dropped every intro price on the new pages — caught before deploy.
- Minecraft was the one active family missing from `PREVIEW_GAMES` (its own page predates this template) — added a `MINECRAFT` entry from real seeded `GamePlan` data.
- A live "a American audience" a/an grammar bug (the exact class flagged) was found in 5 sentences across `gameLocationLandings.ts`, including on the currently-live general per-location pages — fixed with a small `articleFor()` helper.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean throughout. Real Playwright checks (desktop + mobile) on `/rust-server-hosting` (confirmed byte-identical, no locationNote, original "Singapore · low latency" chip), `/singapore-minecraft-server-hosting`, `/united-states-rust-server-hosting`, `/north-america-vps-hosting` (confirmed still `UseCaseLanding`), and `/south-korea-valheim-server-hosting` — all 200, real flag PNGs (no emoji), correct three-tier honesty copy ("real datacenter" / "low-latency network" / "audience · served from SG/DE"), centered layout both viewports. Renewal-price disclosure was verified end-to-end live on production (`/united-states-rust-server-hosting`: "$17.99/mo... Intro price for your first term, then $32.38/mo — renews at the regular price").

**Deploy:** Committed in 3 focused commits, staged twice (confirming health both before and after a concurrent NxLabs commit landed on `main`), promoted to production. BUILD_ID confirmed fresh: `7-Ibx9KM9naTBw7ZZ-5TK` → `z9srsQqJaregrBEwT3vre`. All 5 test URLs return 200 live on `nxeon.cloud`. `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` updated with a full change-history entry.

**One noted gap (not fixed, out of scope):** staging's DB (`nxeon_staging`) has zero `GamePlan` rows with `introPriceCents` set — a pre-existing environment drift unrelated to this change — so the renewal-disclosure UI couldn't be screenshotted on staging; it was instead verified directly against real production data (shown above).
